metadata.source: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (DCS), text ID 61. http://www.sanskrit-linguistics.org/dcs/ Segmentation follows the DCS line/pāda boundaries; chapter and verse labels are taken from the DCS references.

children.text: nāradād yāś ca munayo yamaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> and the other sages approached <s>Yama</s>, the best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s> (normative order),

children.text: praṇamya sukham āsīnaṃ vṛddhaṃ jñānavidāṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: bowed to him as he sat at ease, aged and foremost among those who know wisdom.
They asked about Vedic action, beneficial to all worlds,
destroying all sin, great through hearing and knowledge.
"Great sage, I shall declare it," said <s>Yama</s>, not the three-eyed one,
having gathered together the <s>dharmaśāstras</s> (treatises on normative conduct), for the benefit of all worlds.
Having risen from sleep at dawn in the morning, one should sip water and then remember <s>Hara</s>.
After rising, one should void feces and urine in a proper place apart.
Away from the village, in an unobstructed place, covering the ground with grass,

children.text: śiraḥ prāvṛtya vastreṇa pidhāyāsyaṃ kareṇa ca ||
children.translated_text: covering the head with a garment and covering the mouth with the hand,
one should pass feces and urine facing north and the like at the two twilights.
By day one should do it facing north; by night facing south, or in the direction of <s>Hari</s>.
In the forenoon one faces west; in the afternoon one faces the direction of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: na kedāre na setau ca nāśucau na ca bhūruhe ||
children.translated_text: Not in a field, not on an embankment, not in an impure place, and not on a tree.
One who rinses the mouth, urinates,

children.text: dantaśuddhiṃ ca yaḥ kuryāt pacyate narakādinā ||
children.translated_text: or cleans the teeth near a river or temple is cooked in hell and the like.
Rising while holding the penis, silent and wrapped in a garment,

children.text: pūrvam uddhṛtatoyena śaucaṃ kuryāt tathā mṛdā ||
children.translated_text: one should first perform cleansing with water drawn up beforehand, and likewise with earth.
One should not take earth for cleansing from a road-place, an anthill, saline ground, or what has been heaped by mice,

children.text: nānyaśiṣṭāṃ ca nārdrāṃ ca śaucārthaṃ mṛdam āharet ||
children.translated_text: nor earth left by another, nor wet earth.

children.text: gudeṣṭābhir dvādaśabhiḥ mṛdbhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiś ca vā
children.translated_text: For the anus, with twelve lumps of earth, or with sixteen,
or even with twenty-four, or else with thirty-two,

children.text: nyūnādhikān akartavyā asaṃkhyāś ca vṛthā bhavet
children.translated_text: one should not make them fewer or more; uncounted applications become fruitless.

children.text: yāvad gandhakṣayo vāpi śaucaṃ kuryād viśuddhaye ||
children.translated_text: Or one should cleanse until the smell is gone, for purification.
One should clean the beginning and end, and the place of cleansing, day and night.

children.text: nocet pitṝn bhakṣayati svayaṃ cāśucitāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise he consumes the ancestors and himself falls into impurity.

children.text: liṅgeti saḥ kare vāme daśāsapta ca dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: For the organ, so it is said, and on the left hand ten and seven on the right,
on the feet seven or three, with earth the size of an āmalaka fruit.

children.text: aivaṃ malavisarge tu mūtraśauce tu kathyate
children.translated_text: Thus for evacuation of feces; now cleansing after urine is stated.

children.text: ekāliṅge kare tisraḥ dve vā pañca ca hastayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Once for the organ, three times for the hand, or two or five times for the hands.

children.text: savyahastaṃ bahir jānau apaśyaiva tad antarā
children.translated_text: Keeping the left hand outside the knee, without looking between them,

children.text: evaṃ śocaṃ dvijaḥ kṛtvā ājānukṣālayet pade ||
children.translated_text: having thus performed cleansing, a twice-born man should wash the feet up to the knees.

children.text: śaucamitthaṃ gṛhasthasya varṇī tu dviguṇaṃ caret
children.translated_text: Such is the cleansing for a householder; a religious student should perform twice as much,

children.text: triguṇaṃ tu vanasthasya yatīnāṃ tu caturguṇam ||
children.translated_text: a forest-dweller three times as much, and ascetics four times as much.

children.text: strīśūdrāṇāṃ yathā śocaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca manaḥ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: For women and śūdras, cleansing is according to capacity; for all, purity of mind is required.

children.text: kṛtvā dvādaśagaṇḍūṣaṃ malasūtre tu ṣaḍ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having made twelve mouth-rinsings, after feces and urine there should be six.

children.text: praveśayet karaṃ savyaṃ jale cāmaṇi bandhanam
children.translated_text: He should put the left hand into the water up to the bracelet-joint,
then, facing east, he should drink water with the right hand.

children.text: samantrakam aśabdaṃ ca hṛdayasthe jale punaḥ
children.translated_text: With mantra, without sound, when the water is placed at the heart again,
with the thumb and ring-finger he should touch the twelve limbs.

children.text: madhye madhye jalaṃ spṛśya tattad evaṃ su cintayet
children.translated_text: Touching water in between, he should carefully meditate on each respective thing in this way.

children.text: parimṛśya dvir āsyaṃ tu sakṛd oṣṭhau parispṛśet ||
children.translated_text: Having wiped the mouth twice, he should touch the lips once.
Reciting the three Vedas, he should drink water the measure of a bean.

children.text: tvaṃ nyūnam adhikaṃ pītaṃ sureti kavayo viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: If less or more is drunk, the learned know it to be liquor.

children.text: vyāhṛtībhiś caturvāraṃ triḥ pibet praṇavena vā
children.translated_text: With the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> he should drink three times, or four times with the <s>praṇava</s>,

children.text: sāvitryā va pibed ambū triḥ pibed vāpy āmantrakam ||
children.translated_text: or he should drink water with the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, three times, or even without mantra.
Making the hand like a cow's ear, he should take water from the divine tīrtha of the hand.

children.text: pibe ca brahmatīrthe na divā vīkṣya jalaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: He should drink at the brahma-tīrtha, and by day should drink after looking at the water.

children.text: pibed vipro jale hyasthe karmasthe bāhujaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: A Brāhmaṇa is purified by water reaching the heart; a Kṣatriya again by water reaching the throat,

children.text: vaiśyāśūdrās tathā nārya āsyasthe ca punāti ca ||
children.translated_text: and Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and women by water reaching the mouth.
A Brāhmaṇa wearing a <s>pavitra</s> (sacred grass ring) should perform pure ācamana.
In Vedic rites the <s>pavitra</s> must not be abandoned; otherwise, it is like one's own offspring.
At the time of ritual it should have the scent of brahman; at mealtime it should be round.
The Brāhmaṇa's <s>pavitra</s> is made with four shoots of darbha grass.

children.text: ekaikaṃ nyūnam uddiṣṭaṃ varṇe varṇe yathā kramam
children.translated_text: For each varṇa in order, one less is prescribed.

children.text: dantaśuddhiṃ tataḥ kuryād dantakāṣṭhaiḥ śubhaiḥ samaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one should clean the teeth with auspicious, even tooth-sticks.
One should use those produced from milky trees, or else from thorny trees.

children.text: kāghāsaiḥ kramukaiḥ kāśaiḥ kharguraś ca niṣiddhajaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Grasses, areca, kāśa, date-palm, and prohibited kinds are to be avoided.

children.text: na kurddantasi śuddhyaṃ ca kṛtvā sadyo tyajo bhavet
children.translated_text: One should not do tooth-cleansing with what is improper; having done so, one would at once become fallen.
It should be done in clockwise order, with a gentle instrument.
On the first lunar day, the bhūta-sixth, the ninths, and on parvan days,
if tooth-cleaning is done on a śrāddha day, it burns one's family up to the seventh generation.
On the seventh, under an eclipsed or darkened sun, at Śravaṇa, or on one's birthday,
one should not perform tooth-cleansing then; instead one should do twelve mouth-rinsings.
In the eastern quarter one obtains prosperity; in the northeastern, all accomplishments.
Elsewhere there is great fault, causing loss of sons, wife, and cattle.

children.text: evaṃ dantānūśucī kṛtvā punar ācamya buddhimān
children.translated_text: Having thus made the teeth clean, the wise man should again perform ācamana,

children.text: saṃkalpya vidhipūrvaṃ tu tataḥ snātum upakramet ||
children.translated_text: and, having made the resolve according to rule, he should then begin to bathe.
Resolve, permission, ācamana, worship, and aghamarṣaṇa,
and also the offering to the gods and others: bathing is said to have five limbs.
Having mentioned the lunar day, weekday, and the rest, using the divine tīrtha and kuśa grass,

children.text: āpo hiṣṭheti tisṛbhiḥ mārjayen mūrdhni vāṣṭabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with the three verses beginning āpo hi ṣṭhā, or with eight, he should sprinkle the head.
The Apadhūpta, Kāruvaṇa, Puruṣa-sūkta, and Rudra-sūkta,
the Śrī-sūkta, Bhūmi-sūkta, and Sūrya-sūkta he should duly perform.
And having recited the <s>Viṣṇu-gāyatrī</s>, and likewise the mantra of eight syllables afterward,

children.text: kāveryās tu sakṛt toyair brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: with the waters of the <s>Kāverī</s> even once he drives away the sin of brahmahatyā.
Then, saying the prescribed utterance, he should satisfy the ancestors, gods, sages, and twice-born.
When, with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> furnished with <s>oṃ</s> and the vyāhṛtis, and with its head-formula,
he takes water, recites, and then once casts it upon his head,
the sin acquired over ten births perishes at that very moment.
Then, having come out, he should shake out a clean garment; the text here is corrupt around the instruction for shaking it.
'The shaken-off one is protected; the enemies are shaken off' - so the damaged mantra appears to say.

children.text: sūrye pradarśyo dityam iti devasya tveti gṛhya ca
children.translated_text: He should show it to the sun, with the formula beginning 'to the Āditya,' and take it with 'of the god, for thee,'
put it on, then, after sipping water twice, he should deal with the wet garment; the wording is damaged.

children.text: prokṣayitvā nipī ayāyaṃ yekeceti ca maṃtrataḥ
children.translated_text: Having sprinkled it, and with the mantra beginning 'whatever here,' the text gives a further damaged instruction for drinking or purifying,

children.text: vāma? prakoṣṭhe nikṣipya dvir ācamya viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: he should place it on the left forearm, sip water twice, and so becomes purified.
Again sipping water, making the resolve, and preceded by prāṇāyāma,

children.text: āpo hiṣṭhādibhir maṃtraiḥ śīrasi prokṣayej jalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should sprinkle water on his head with the mantras beginning 'āpo hi ṣṭhā.'

children.text: vyastamaṃtrair viśudhya syāt samastai brahmahā bhavet
children.translated_text: By the separate mantras he becomes pure; by the combined ones even a slayer of a Brahmin is purified.

children.text: na prokṣayet xironyatra brahmahatyāṃ sa viṃdati ||
children.translated_text: He should not sprinkle the head elsewhere; if he does so, he incurs brahmahatyā.
He should sip water with the mantra 'sūryaś ca,' and wipe himself with 'dadhikrāvaṇ.'
Then, taking water with both hands and meditating on <s>Nṛcāhari</s>,
and consecrating it with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, he should, while standing with feet joined,

children.text: mūrdhaṃtriḥ prakṣiped arghyaṃ kṛtvā gośṛṃgavat karau ||
children.translated_text: cast the arghya three times on his head, making his hands like the horn of a cow.

children.text: ādityābhimukhas tv arghyaṃ datvā tīraṃsam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: Facing the sun, having given the arghya, and having returned to the bank,
he should sprinkle himself with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and circumambulate with the formula beginning 'asau.'

children.text: saṃtārpya keśavādīṃś ca gṛhānś cācamya vai kramāt
children.translated_text: Having satisfied <s>Keśava</s> and the others, and the planetary powers, he should sip water in order.

children.text: upaviśya śucau deśo prā mukheṣv āsaneṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: Sitting in a pure place, on seats facing east,

children.text: ṛṣiśchaṃdaḥ svarāṃ spṛtvā prāṇāyāmam athā caret
children.translated_text: having touched the seers, metres, and accents, he should then perform prāṇāyāma.
He should recite three times the <s>Gāyatrī</s> together with the vyāhṛtis and <s>oṃ</s>, along with the head-formula,

children.text: triḥ paṭhen niyatāt māyaḥ prāṇāyāmam ixṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: with controlled self; this they know as prāṇāyāma.
By inhalation he draws it upward and holds it in the region indicated; the wording is partly corrupt.
Then by retention he spreads through all the limbs the accumulated mass of hostile sins,
and by exhalation, bringing it together, he places it in the right hand.

children.text: tat pāpaṃ tu kṣiped bhūmau coravaṃtī charaṃtakaḥ
children.translated_text: He should cast that sin upon the ground, like a thief being driven away; the end of the line is corrupt.
The place of the head of the Gāyatrī of the syllables is declared; the line is corrupt in its opening.
Whether recited once, or repeated three times, it has great fruit.
When the three prāṇāyāmas are performed, threefold sin is destroyed.

children.text: manasā niṣṭaciṃtāś ca pareṣāṃ ca tathāśane
children.translated_text: Sins consisting in evil thoughts in the mind, and likewise in eating what belongs to others,
he should cause the wind to raise up into fire; by fire the sin is burned away.
Through the breath-wind and exhalation he should perform the three prāṇāyāmas.
In rites of divine oblation, in the acts of recitation and meditation,
one should perform the three prāṇāyāmas; this is the injunction of the Veda.

children.text: ādyaṃ tayos tu gāyatryā prāṇāyāmatrayaṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning of those rites one should perform the three prāṇāyāmas with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
In the middle, four are prescribed, and ten praṇavas are stated.
At the time of sandhyā-vandana, for the arghya, one prāṇāyāma is prescribed.
The method of prāṇāyāma should be with the middle fingers and the other thumbs; the wording is compressed.
With the joining of the middle and index fingers, however, a Brahmin becomes impure.
Making both hands furnished with pavitras, he should perform the three prāṇāyāmas,
and, remembering the gods, seers, and metres, he should then perform purification of the elements.
He should raise the breath, filling his own belly; the beginning of the line is corrupt.
If he should separate it through the throat, he is regarded as the supreme yogin; the line is damaged.

children.text: daśādhāmātṛkā nyāsān kuryād vipro yathā balaṃ
children.translated_text: A Brahmin should perform the ten placements of the mātṛkā-syllables according to his ability.
Or, having performed the pure mātṛkā up to its completion, preceded by meditation,
he should then recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> ten times with prāṇāyāma.
With the anuvāka beginning 'āyātu,' he should invoke the mother of the Veda.
The recollection of the sage of the sound-Brahman belongs to the pure mātṛkā.
The deity is said to be three-footed, and is employed for the meaning of the mātṛkā.
The syllables beginning with ka, joined with the initial and final vowels and with anusvāra,
known from ya onward up to kṣa, should be placed upon the limbs of the body; the line is corrupt.
On the head, face, and movements, and on both auspicious eyes and ears,
on the nose, the pair of lips, and below at the damaged place named in the text, the twice-born should place them.

children.text: punarmūrdhnimux nyais yā ṣo aśāpi svarāḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: Again on the head and mouth he should place in order the sixteen vowels as well.

children.text: vinyasec caturaḥ kādīn karavatyaṃ ca saviṣu ||
children.translated_text: He should place the four groups beginning with ka on the arms and on the other parts; the wording is corrupt.
On the sides, back, and navel, and with care on the purifying parts, he should perform the placement.
At the root of the heart, the throat or kakut, the armpits, and the pair of hands of the heart,
and on the belly and face he should make the placement that removes sin; the wording is damaged.

children.text: paṃcāśatkarmabheder vihitavadanopādayukkukṣipakṣadehāṃ bhāsvatkavardākalitaśasikalām iṇdukudāvadātāṃ .akṣasvatkuṃbhaciṃtālikhitavarakarāṃ tryakṣarāṃ padmahastām achākalpa .atujastanabharanamitāṃ bhāraṃtītvāṃ namāmi ||
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Bhāratī</s>, whose form is connected with the fifty ritual divisions, whose bright body has face, feet, belly, and sides, who bears the crescent digit of the moon, white like the moon and jasmine, whose fine hands hold rosary, pitcher, thought, and writing, three-syllabled, lotus-handed, with breasts bending beneath their weight: I bow to you.'

children.text: dhyātvaivaṃ mātṛkāṃ śuddhām athāṃ tamātṛkā nyaset
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated on the pure mātṛkā, he should then place the inner mātṛkā.

children.text: ādhāreli ganābhau hṛdayasarasijekarṇamūle lalāṭe devatreṣo aśāredvidaśadaśada e dvādaśārddhe catuṣkebāsāṃte bālamadhye phakaṭasahite karṇamadhye svarāṇāṃ bhakṣaṃ tatvārthayuktaṃ sakalada ayutaṃ varṇarūpaṃ namāmi ||
children.translated_text: 'In the support, the liṅga, the navel, the lotus of the heart, the root of the ears, and the forehead, in the divine three, the sixteen-spoked, the twice-ten and ten-spoked, the twelve-half and fourfold places, at the end of the nose, between the brows, with pha and kaṭa, in the middle of the ear among the vowels: I honor the syllabic form, joined with the meaning of reality and composed of all the groups.'
